claims.text: The Liskov Substitution Principle: code that uses a base type must work correctly, without change, when given objects of any of its subtypes.
claims.source_hint: glossary entry lsp; standard formulation in software design literature

claims.text: ShippingFee declares abstract int ForOrder(int totalVnd); StandardShipping returns 0 from 2,000,000 else 30,000, ExpressShipping 60,000, PickUpInStore 0 — each returns an int for every int input and none throws.

EveryKindAnswersTheSameCall builds a ShippingFee[] of the three kinds and asserts that ForOrder(2_000_000) on each gives {0, 60000, 0}; SamplesTests.cs is the only code at stage-0 that calls ForOrder.
The C# compiler checks that an override matches the base method's signature; C# has no checked exceptions, so it does not check whether a method throws for some inputs.
claims.source_hint: C# language reference: override, exceptions (no checked exceptions)

claims.text: ForOrder(500_000) returns 30000 for StandardShipping, 60000 for ExpressShipping and 0 for PickUpInStore.
A hypothetical FreeShippingOnly that returns 0 from 2,000,000 and throws below would pass EveryKindAnswersTheSameCall if added with expected 0, since the test only calls ForOrder(2_000_000).
A subtype that throws for inputs the base type's method accepts breaks substitution: callers written for the base type are no longer correct for it.
claims.source_hint: outline item 3; follows from the LSP definition

claims.text: Implementing every abstract method is enforced by the compiler and is not what LSP adds; LSP concerns behaviour.
claims.source_hint: C# compiler error CS0534 (non-abstract class must implement inherited abstract members); outline misconception 1

self_check.notes: Outline item 2's 'one call site' is the test EveryKindAnswersTheSameCall, so SamplesTests.cs was added to example_files. FreeShippingOnly is hypothetical (outline item 3) and described in prose only, no code block. No variance or formal pre/post-conditions, per depth_notes.
